threads.thread_goal: Align on current pain points and approve target tax workflow scope.

messages.text: Hello team! Kicking off our project: Standardised Tax Documentation & Filing Workflow Rollout. The main goal is to create a clear, audit-ready process for everyone. First step is mapping the current state as per T1. I'll be reaching out to schedule time with a few departments to understand their existing workflows. Any initial thoughts on where the biggest pain points are?

Thanks for kicking this off. From a tax perspective, the biggest challenge is inconsistent data formats and late submissions from different departments. This creates a lot of rework right before deadlines. We need to ensure the new workflow map A1 is very specific about handover requirements.
I agree. The data from Finance and Operations is usually the most complex. Maybe we should start the T1 mapping with them to tackle the hardest part first?
So for T1 we are only talking to Finance and Ops? What about Accounting?

Good question. Yes, we definitely need Accounting. Let's agree to limit the initial scope to Finance, Operations, and Accounting. This will help us build a solid foundation before expanding. Does that sound good for our initial scope?

Yes, that's a sensible scope. D1 confirmed. As we build out the workflow map A1 and the RACI matrix for T4, we need to ensure there's a single owner for maintaining these documents to prevent version control issues.

We should also consider the implications for inter-company transactions. The data reconciliation process for those is often managed outside the standard departmental workflows and can be a major source of discrepancies during consolidation. The current process maps probably don't capture this nuance, which could be a risk.

That's a very important point, thanks for raising it. Let's add that as a specific area to investigate during the T1 interviews. For now, I can take ownership of maintaining the A1 workflow map and the A5 RACI matrix to ensure consistency. Is everyone aligned with that?
Works for me. Thanks for taking that on.
Confirmed. D2 is set. Having one owner is crucial.

threads.thread_goal: Design and sign off templates, tracker, and checklist for tax documentation.

messages.text: Hi all, I've created the first drafts for the tax documentation templates as part of T2. I've also mocked up a structure for the centralized tracker A2, which is part of T3. Please review and provide feedback. The goal is to make them clear and easy for everyone to use.

Thanks! Looking at the A2 tracker, the structure is clean. One suggestion: could we add a column for 'Data Source System' e.g., SAP, Oracle? This would be incredibly helpful for tracing back numbers during an audit and would streamline the validation process.
The templates for T2 look great. They cover all the main areas and the instructions are straightforward. I don't have any changes to suggest.
Excellent point. That will definitely add value for audit trails. I'll add that column to the A2 structure. Let's consider that part of the agreed design.
Sorry if this is a silly question, but I don't see a template for our team's monthly expense reports. Which one should we use for that?
Not a silly question at all. That would fall under the 'Deductible Expenses Summary' template. I'll add a note in the description to make that clearer. Thanks for flagging.

Regarding the 'Data Source System' column, we need to be careful about defining what we mean. Some data comes from direct system exports, but other figures are the result of manual consolidation in secondary spreadsheets. How do we label those? If we aren't precise, the column could create more confusion than clarity.

Good point. We can create a simple data validation rule for that column: either a system name or 'Manual Consolidation'. That keeps it simple but accurate. While we're on templates, should we also create a simple Pre-Filing Tax Documentation Checklist A4 based on these new documents? It would help ensure nothing is missed before submission.

I like both suggestions. A dropdown for the source system in A2 is a great idea, and I was already planning to draft the A4 checklist, so this is perfect timing. With the clarification for expenses and the tracker structure agreed, I think we can approve the templates for T2. Any objections?
No objections from me. Approved.
All good here. Let's move forward.
Great. D3 and D4 are confirmed. I'll finalize the templates and start on the A4 checklist. Thanks for the excellent feedback everyone.

threads.thread_goal: Lock roles, responsibilities, and reminder/escalation rules.

messages.text: Hi team, as part of T4, I've drafted the RACI matrix A5 for the new workflow. I've also put together a proposal for the reminder and escalation rules for T9 to help us get data on time. Please take a look and let me know your thoughts.

Thanks. Reviewing A5, there's one critical adjustment needed. For the 'Final Review and Sign-off' step, the Tax Compliance Officer must be 'Accountable', not just 'Consulted'. This is a non-negotiable from a compliance standpoint.

Good catch. I agree with that change. For the T9 reminders, the 3-day warning is good, but I suggest the escalation to the department head happens on the due date itself, not two days after. A delay in escalation reduces the urgency and we might still get the data late.
In the escalation plan, who is the contact person for the Marketing department? It's not listed.
Ah, thanks for spotting that omission. I'll get the name of the Marketing manager and add it to the list. I'll also make the changes suggested by @66260 and @109659.
Perfect. @60334 do you have any feedback on the A5 or T9 drafts?
The overall structure seems fine to me.

Great. So, to summarize, I will update A5 to set the Tax Officer as 'Accountable' and adjust the T9 escalation to trigger on the due date. With these changes, can we consider the RACI matrix approved (D5) and the reminder plan confirmed (D6)?
Yes, approved from my side.
Agreed. Let's lock it in.
Excellent. D5 and D6 are now confirmed. I'll publish the final versions by tomorrow morning.

threads.thread_goal: Plan and debrief the pilot run of the new workflow.

messages.text: Team, let's plan the pilot for T7. I propose we use next month's VAT filing. It's a recurring process that involves multiple departments, making it a good test case without the high pressure of a quarterly corporate tax filing. What are your thoughts?
That's a great choice for the pilot scope. It will give us valuable feedback from Sales and Operations on the new templates and handovers. I support this selection.
Sounds good. What is the exact cut-off date for the data we'll be using in this pilot run?

The cut-off will be the 5th of next month. I've also drafted the incident handling procedure for T12 and will use the A7 log to track any issues we encounter. So, are we agreed on the VAT filing for the pilot?
Yes, confirmed. D7 is set.

Hi all, quick update: the pilot for T7 is now complete. It was largely successful, but we captured a couple of key feedback points in the A7 log. The main one is that the guidelines in A3 need a more detailed example for inter-departmental data handovers. The current description was a bit too generic.
I also had some trouble finding the correct template to use. It would be helpful if we could click a link in the tracker to open the right template directly.
That's a fantastic usability suggestion, @543897. We can easily add hyperlinks to the templates in the A2 tracker. @66260, based on this feedback, what's the plan for T8?

The plan for T8 is to incorporate this feedback. Specifically: 1. I will update the A3 guidelines with a clear, step-by-step example. 2. We will add hyperlinks to the templates in the A2 tracker. These seem to be the main adjustments needed. Shall we agree on these changes?
Sounds like a solid plan. I can take care of adding the hyperlinks to the tracker once the templates are finalized.
Perfect. Then D8 is confirmed. I'll also start structuring the A8 Post-Rollout report so we're ready to collect metrics once we go live.

threads.thread_goal: Coordinate training sessions and final rollout communication.

messages.text: Hi everyone, I've put together the draft training slides A6 for T6 and a proposed rollout timeline. I've tentatively scheduled two sessions next week targeting the Finance and Operations teams. Are there any other groups we should make sure to include?

The slides in A6 look good, they cover the key changes well. For the training sessions, we must make attendance mandatory for the Finance Manager's direct reports. They handle the final data consolidation, so their adoption is critical.
We should probably invite the administrative assistants from the Legal department too. They often provide supporting contracts and documents for tax purposes and should be aware of the new process.
Both great points. I'll update the invite list to include Legal and will mark the session for the Finance team as mandatory. That should settle the attendee groups.
When will the final version of the A3 guidelines be available for us to read before the training?

I'm applying the final touches based on the pilot feedback. The updated A3 will be published by EOD today, well ahead of the training sessions. I'm also doing a final check on the T11 statutory books alignment.

Looking at the proposed timeline, the buffer between the last training session and the go-live date is only one day. This seems risky. It doesn't leave any room to address follow-up questions or make minor adjustments based on feedback from the training.

That's a very valid concern, @60334. You're right, we should build in more of a buffer. I propose we push the go-live date by two business days. This will give us time to breathe and ensure a smoother launch. How does everyone feel about that?
A safer approach. I agree. This also gives us a cleaner start date for collecting the metrics for the T10 post-rollout report.
Excellent. Then we have our decisions. D9 and D10 are confirmed. I will update the official project timeline and send out the finalized training invitations this afternoon.
